newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says will sell Iran 50,000 T sugar.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says will sell Iran 50,000 T sugar.

text.p: Turkey has agreed with Iran to sell it 50,000 tonnes of sugar from its stocks and more sugar exports might come later, a senior industry ministry official said on Monday.

"We have stocks this year. We will sell the surplus. Our colleagues have had talks with Iranian officials and they agreed to sell 50,000 tonnes," Ersen Yavuz, industry ministry undersecretary, told Reuters in an interview.
He said Iranian officials told them Iran needed 600,000 tonnes of sugar in 1997.
"I asked my colleagues at Turkseker to arrange for further sugar sales to Iran," he said. He did not give other details.

Turkey said on Friday its state sugar refineries company, Turkseker, planned to export 300,000 tonnes of sugar in calendar 1997 from its surplus, and added the sales would be mainly to Azerbaijan, Georgia and Uzbekistan.
A crowded Iranian delegation, headed by President Akbar Hashimi Rafsanjani and including senior ministers and officials, left Turkey on Sunday after a four-day visit.
Turkey is expected to produce 1.85 million tonnes of sugar in 1996/97, and total sugar supply will exceed two million tonnes including stocks at private companies.

Turkey has also offered to sell Iraq 50,000 tonnes of sugar under a U.N. oil-for-food deal which allows Iraq to sell oil worth $2 billion over six months to buy food and medicine. --Ercan Ersoy, Ankara Newsroom 90-312-4462940
